Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

house — a building where a family lives. Example: We live in a small house.
flat — a home on one floor of a building. Example: My flat is on the second floor.
apartment — a home in a larger building. Example: She rents an apartment in the city.
street — a road with houses or shops. Example: I live on Mill Street.
city — a large town. Example: Rome is a big city.
town — a place smaller than a city. Example: I live in a small town.
village — a very small place in the country. Example: The village has one shop.
neighbourhood — the area around your home. Example: My neighbourhood is quiet.
live — to have your home somewhere. Example: I live in Lisbon.
near — close to. Example: The shop is near my house.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I live in...
• I live on ... Street.
• It is near the...
• My neighbourhood is quiet.
• Is it far from here?

elements.content: Stress the place word, not the preposition.
I live in ROME. My house is on MILL Street.
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: Prepositions of place (in, on, near).
Use in for towns, cities and countries, on for streets, and near for distance: I live in Rome. I live on Green Street. My flat is near the park.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct preposition: I live ___ Rome.
Choose the correct sentence.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
I live in a small town near Bristol. My house is on Mill Street. There is a park near my house and a shop near the station.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: Where do you live? B: I live in a flat in the city centre. A: Is it near the station? B: Yes, it is very near.
